_comment: The files under website/atlas/ that scripts/build-atlas-pages.py must NEVER delete or overwrite.
Two kinds: hand-written 'spine' sheets (class="spine") that exist nowhere in data/repertoire.js,
and small meta-refresh stubs kept so URLs already shared keep working.
Detect drift with:  grep -l 'class="spine"' website/atlas/*.html   and   grep -l 'http-equiv="refresh"' website/atlas/*.html
A hand-written sheet MUST also be pinned open — otherwise the build would print 'Not open yet' on a page that already carries the full research, which is a lie on the page itself.
_hubCards_comment: Only for crafts that exist as a hand-written sheet but have no record in data/repertoire.js, so the browse home can show them a card. Every field transcribed verbatim from the sheet itself — nothing invented.

hubCards.blurb: The blade that lost its war in 1876 and moved to the kitchen — and the one souvenir you're meant to use until it wears out. In a day at a real fire you hammer the guided steps while a master keeps the dangerous ones, and you carry home a single-bevel knife you helped forge.
hubCards.why: A working forge on the Shimanto river in Tosa blade country, where you forge, grind and harden your own blade in the quench — the part most places keep for themselves.

hubCards.blurb: The one craft here sold as walking away from everyone — whose own founder said its whole point was to end up needing them. Growing your own food, and keeping it through the winter, is real skill: soil, water, seed, and a preservation craft where a mistake can genuinely poison you.
hubCards.why: Sunseed isn't a course you attend; it's a small off-grid community you move into — and the living scene is the lesson, not a demonstration of one.

hubCards.blurb: Nobody's country decides whether you're qualified to cook at sea — the flag on the transom does, and it usually asks for less than the schools do. A trade, not a tradition: no master, no workshop, no line of teachers. It passes between chefs who overlap for a season, aboard.
hubCards.school: Anchor & Apron — Cara Whiteman & Amber Colle
hubCards.why: Two experienced yacht chefs who came off the boats to teach their own trade, on published dates, with three days and nights aboard a catamaran. The craft has no lineage to inherit — this is people who do the job, teaching it.
hubCards.tripLength: three days to two weeks, or no travel at all

_craftFamilies_comment: Curated adjacency for the 'Close to this on the map' block on every craft page. Hand-grouped on purpose: a scored similarity pass paired Muay Thai with Thai massage on the word 'Thai'. A craft may sit in several families; the builder takes one from each in turn. Every craft must be in at least one family or the build stops.
_learnLines_comment: The immersive line under the place name on every craft page's place card, keyed by DESTINATION id. Hand-written, for the same reason craftFamilies is hand-grouped: every attempt to compose one from the craft blurb plus the destination's `why` read as a machine talking. And compressing a researched sentence is exactly where a claim quietly changes — 'the most photographed big-cat ground on earth' is NOT 'where the most big cats are', and only one of those is true. RULE: a line here may say nothing its own `why` does not already say. Where a destination is a heritage source with no vouched school, or is an experts-only spot, the line must NOT begin 'Learn to' — it would promise teaching that is not there. A missing line is fine: the card simply shows none. See LEARN_LINES in build-atlas-pages.py.

_sayLines_comment: The FIRST line a card says, keyed by DESTINATION id. Where learnLines is the researched sentence, this is the card's own title: 'Learn to photograph big cats from a camp' with 'in Kenya' on the line under it. At rest a card names the craft — 'Learn Wildlife Photography in Pusztaszer, Hungary' — and while it walks its places this replaces the craft's name with what you would actually be doing in THAT one. Write it against the destination's WHOLE record, not just its `why`: schoolsInfo carries the course and the school's own blurb, which is where 'one-way glass', 'on the Russian border' and 'four to a group' come from. Three rules. It may say nothing that record does not already say (gated by learn_line_drift). Where there is no vouched school it must not begin 'Learn to' — that would promise teaching that is not there. And it never carries the place: the card prints the place on the next line and would say it twice. Length is free — the card reserves the height of the longest line it can ever show — but short is the point of the line. A missing line is fine: the card keeps naming the craft. See SAY_LINES in build-atlas-pages.py.

_measure_comment: The Measure — the per-craft answer to the promise the trust block already makes: what we check before we send you anywhere. Five questions on the five dots, asked in the same words and the same order on every craft, because a legend a reader has to relearn is not a legend (the build refuses any other wording — see MEASURE_QUESTIONS in scripts/atlas_hub.py). The instrument's own shorthand — the room, the door, the bench, the ground, the stretch — stays in THE-MEASURE-META-PROMPT.md and never reaches a reader: on the page we ask the question rather than name it. Rendered only for crafts listed here; a craft with no entry shows no meter, which is an absence and not a zero. Desk research stops at three — whether a craft is alive in its place, and whether there is enough there to keep you going, are exactly what a brochure claims, and only somebody standing in the room settles them. Never write a line that ranks one craft against another, and never borrow a restaurant guide's award language: we report what we found and hand the reader the decision.

modernist-spanish-cuisine.verdict: If this craft already pulls you, there is enough here to go on — we have not stood in it, so we will not tell you to cross the world for it yet

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Martín Lippo teaches modernist technique in his own Barcelona laboratory — a named person, in his own working place. Madrid's route is institutional rather than personal: Le Cordon Bleu inside the Universidad Francisco de Vitoria, with no single teacher named on it.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: You can book your way in, on dates. Madrid's avant-garde teaching is the last third of a nine-month Spanish Cuisine Diploma, and their own syllabus names the block — spherifications, low-temperature cooking, the fundamentals of molecular cuisine. Barcelona's lab courses are shorter. The stage is the other road and it is a real one, but it is applied for with a CV and nobody can promise you one: only one of the two is a way in you can book. Your hands can ruin the work on either.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: The strongest thing this craft has — and the community dots above are the evidence for it, not a second opinion. Barcelona is where the elBulli cooks actually landed, and Disfrutar, opened by three of them, was named the world's best restaurant in 2024. Madrid gathers the whole avant-garde once a year at Madrid Fusión, running since 2003 and reaching its 25th edition in February 2027. There is a generation above you here, and one below.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and this is the question that separates this craft from the travelling toolkit. Madrid Fusión — Alimentos de España — has been the vanguard's own congress since 2003, and it happens here rather than in any of the places the technique has since reached. That technique goes anywhere; this cuisine came from here and still argues with itself in the same rooms.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and there is more here than an attendance certificate: the Superior Certificate is a real nine-month qualification, and a stage in a kitchen of this lineage is months on the line. As high as this craft goes is very high — three Michelin stars at DiverXO, the world's best restaurant list at Disfrutar.

modernist-spanish-cuisine.check: Read from the entries already verified on this page, not from a fresh sweep. Nobody from EducatedTraveler has stood in either room — and that alone is what holds the last one, not doubt about the places. When somebody does, the line will carry their name and the day they went. The fourth answer is new: Madrid Fusión's own site, read 4 September 2026.

ashtanga-yoga.verdict: The lineage is intact and the doors are open, but the man this map's pick was named after died in 2024 and access is now a lottery — go in knowing both

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Named, and the naming has changed. R. Sharath Jois died on 11 November 2024 at fifty-three; the Sharath Yoga Centre continues and now names Shruthi Jois and Shraddha Jois. In New York, Eddie Stern teaches at his own shala — a named person in his own room, which is the whole test. London's three Mysore-style programmes name nobody on this page, and should.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open, and unusually honest about being hard. Mysore is a lottery: registration for the 2026 season is closed and students are selected 'randomly by algorithm to match our shala capacity'. London and New York run daily self-practice programmes you can simply join. Your hands can ruin it in the only way this craft allows — by forcing a posture your body has not reached.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Mysore reads Legendary on the community dots above, and learning beside other people is the point of the method: Mysore-style means a room of people practising their own sequence beside you with one teacher moving between them. There is a generation above you here and one below, in three cities.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and not on a school's say-so. Karnataka's own tourism department publishes a page on Mysuru's Ashtanga yoga — “the city has a worldwide recognition as a yoga destination” — and names the shalas on it, the K. Pattabhi Jois Ashtanga Yoga Institute among them. A state naming the practice among the things its city is known for is a town organised around a craft, which is what this question asks. What it cannot tell you is what a season in Gokulam is actually like.

evidence.what: Karnataka Tourism — the state department's own page on Mysuru

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and this is the craft where the ladder matters most and is least settled. Authorisation and then Certification were historically the rarest stamps in yoga and they were Sharath's to give. What they mean now is a question for the shala, and not one we can answer for you.

cold-exposure-wim-hof-method.verdict: One method, one family, one certificate that the same company writes and marks — everything here is real and almost all of it comes from a single source, which you should weigh

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Named at the top: Wim Hof himself takes the Module III intensive in the Karkonosze mountains, and Enahm Hof runs the Academy from Amsterdam. That is a named person in his own room, and unusually it is the person the method is named after. Iceland names nobody and is delivered by certified instructors rather than by the Academy.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open and laddered: Fundamentals, then Modules I to III, ending in an in-person intensive. You book it. And the hands can ruin it in a way worth stating plainly — this is cold water and breath retention, the failure modes are real, and every serious page about it says never to practise the breathing in or near water.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Przesieka reads Legendary above and Amsterdam Thriving. The cohorts are the method's whole distribution — thousands of certified instructors worldwide came through these rooms, which is a genuine peer network and also the reason to read the next dot carefully.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: We have not been. That is the whole reason this one is empty — not anything we found. And of everything on this map, a Karkonosze winter is the one that cannot be researched — you either stood in the water or you did not.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: The same reason, and there is a second reason worth saying: the qualification here is a Certified Wim Hof Method Instructor, awarded by the Wim Hof Method Academy. The company teaches the method, defines the method, and certifies the teachers of the method. That is not a criticism — it is one closed loop rather than an outside body, and you should price it as such.

french-pastry-and-patisserie.verdict: The clearest ladder on this map sits above rooms whose teachers we cannot name — the qualifications are real and the question of who will be in front of you is still open

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Dark after a second look, and the correction is ours. Frédéric Bau founded this school in 1988 and is Valrhona's creative director — both true, both checkable — but the test is a named person who still stands in the room, and we could not confirm he teaches the courses. This page used to carry Pierre Hermé and Cédric Grolet against Paris. Neither teaches on these programmes, and both names have been taken down. A famous name attached to a school is not a teacher. Ask each school who will be at your bench.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at every price and length: FERRANDI's intensive professional programme at about 24,500 EUR, Le Cordon Bleu's Diplôme de Pâtisserie, Bellouet's three-month formation, and L'École Valrhona's two- and three-day professional courses, which is the cheapest serious way into this craft anywhere. Your hands can ruin it constantly and visibly, which is most of what the training is for.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Paris and Tain-l'Hermitage and Tokyo all read Legendary on the community dots above. This is the craft where the peers are the industry — the same rooms, the same suppliers, and a competition circuit that the whole trade watches.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: We have not been. That is the whole reason this one is empty — not anything we found. And the craft is plainly alive around this one: Valrhona is a chocolate factory with a school attached, in the town it is named after.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: The same reason, and it is a shame, because the ladder here is the clearest on the whole map. The CAP Pâtissier is a French state diploma. The Meilleur Ouvrier de France is a national title with an examination and a collar. Neither is a certificate of attendance and neither is ours to vouch for yet.

hatha-and-vinyasa-yoga.verdict: Four of the strongest yoga towns on earth and not one named teacher between them on this page — in a craft where the teacher is the entire product, that is the gap to close before you book

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Empty in all four places, and in this craft that matters more than in any other on the map. Rishikesh and Mysore carry lineages — Sivananda, Krishnamacharya — and a lineage is not a teacher. Ubud's Yoga Barn and Radiantly Alive, and Encinitas's Soul of Yoga, name nobody here either. A two-hundred-hour training is four weeks of one person's attention: find out whose before you pay, and treat a school that will not tell you as an answer.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Wide open, and the widest on this map: two-hundred-hour teacher trainings run continuously in Rishikesh, Mysore, Ubud and Encinitas, residential, with dates published months out. Your hands can ruin it, and in this craft the thing they can ruin is you — this is the discipline where being pushed past your range does lasting damage.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Rishikesh and Ubud both read Legendary above. These are towns where the practice is the local economy, which cuts both ways: there are peers everywhere and there is also a great deal of training sold to people who will never teach.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: We have not been. That is the whole reason this one is empty — not anything we found. Rishikesh on the Ganges is a town this practice organises itself around, and a month there is the only way to know which schools are serious.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: The same reason, and here the ladder is genuinely weak — which their own standards say plainly enough that we can quote the shape of it. RYT 200 is obtained 'after completing a 200-hour yoga teacher training registered with Yoga Alliance'; the teaching requirement for it is listed as None; and the cost is a 50 USD one-time application fee plus 65 USD annual membership dues. Yoga Alliance registers you and requires the school to assess you. It does not examine you. That is a register, not a qualification an outside examiner stands behind, and it is worth knowing exactly what you are buying. Read on their Standards for RYT Credentials, 3 September 2026.

italian-cuisine-and-pasta.verdict: A named woman with flour on her hands at one end and a proper culinary school at the other — this craft is in better shape on this map than most

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Alessandra Spisni teaches the professional sfoglia course at La Vecchia Scuola Bolognese, in her own school, and she is the reason Bologna is the pick. That is the test passed exactly: a named person, still working, in the room you would be in. Forlimpopoli and Colorno carry lineages instead — Artusi, Marchesi — and both are dead, which is why they now sit under 'where it comes from' rather than under who teaches.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at three depths: Spisni's professional sfoglia course at about 6,000 EUR, Casa Artusi's shorter sfoglia courses in Forlimpopoli, and ALMA's Italian Pasta Program at Colorno for people who want the institutional route. Your hands can ruin it in the plainest way on this map — the sfoglia is either right or it is not, and the woman across the table will tell you which.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Bologna reads Legendary above. The sfogline are a living trade in that city rather than a heritage act, and the school sits in the middle of it. Colorno reads Thriving on the strength of ALMA, which draws cooks from everywhere.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: We have not been. That is the whole reason this one is empty — not anything we found. Emilia-Romagna is where this craft grew up, and one week in a Bologna kitchen would answer more than a month of reading.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: The same reason. ALMA's Diploma in Italian Cuisine is a real qualification and the sfoglina training at VSB is a trade credential that Bologna itself recognises. We have read both. We have watched nobody finish either.

jewelry-and-goldsmithing.verdict: There is more to go on here than almost anywhere else on this map — but we have not stood at any of these benches, so the last one is still ours to earn, not yours to trust

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Thinly, and we will say so: Gio Carbone at Le Arti Orafe in Florence is the one named person on this page, in the school he founded. The other three destinations are institutions — the Gemological Institute of America, Pforzheim's Goldschmiedeschule, the Indian Institute of Gems & Jewellery — and name nobody. One name out of four lights this dot. It does not make us comfortable.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open in four countries, on published dates: LAO's annual goldsmithing course in Florence, the GIA Graduate Jeweler diploma over 28 weeks in Carlsbad, Studio Jewelers' 24-week programme in New York, Pforzheim's Berufskolleg and Meisterschule, IIGJ's manufacturing diploma in Jaipur. And your hands can ruin the work about as literally as anywhere here — solder floods, a stone chips, the piece is gone.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: The strongest thing this craft has, and the community dots above are the evidence for it rather than a second opinion. Florence and the Carlsbad–New York axis both read Legendary; Pforzheim is a town built around goldsmithing with a Meisterschule at its centre; Jaipur's Johari Bazaar is lapidary and meenakari ateliers working street by street. Four scenes, three continents, peers in all of them.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes for Pforzheim, and only there. The town has a jewellery museum of its own, the Schmuckmuseum Pforzheim — what a place keeps when the trade is the reason it exists rather than an industry that happens to be there. Jaipur and Florence we have taken on their reputations and the schools' own pages, which is not the same standard; an afternoon in either would settle it.

evidence.what: the Schmuckmuseum Pforzheim, the town's jewellery museum

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and there is plainly more here than an attendance certificate: the GIA Graduate Gemologist is a qualification the trade reads, and the German Meister is a state-regulated title with an examination behind it. We have read that on their pages. We have not watched anyone climb it, and until we have, it stays a claim we are repeating rather than one we are making.

kitesurfing.verdict: The most standardised teaching on this map and the least personal — you can book a certified course almost anywhere, and we cannot name a single instructor

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Empty in all three places. Maui, Tarifa and Cabarete carry ten schools between them and not one named teacher on this page. That is partly the shape of the craft — instruction is certified and interchangeable by design, which is a strength for safety and a weakness for this test — and partly our own gap. Ask who your instructor will be and how many hours they have taught; the school will have the answer and the answer varies enormously.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Wider than anywhere else on this map. IKO courses run at every level in all three places, typically three days, in small groups — Freeride Tarifa caps at two to four students an instructor. And the hands can ruin it in a way that is genuinely dangerous rather than merely disappointing, which is why the certification exists at all.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Tarifa and Cabarete both read Legendary above, and they are the two towns in the world where the whole day is organised around wind. The peers are on the water beside you, which in this craft is where learning actually happens.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes. The Global Kitesports Association's own calendar puts the GKA Youth Kite World Championships in Tarifa on 25–28 June 2026 — the tour bringing a world championship to the town, booked by nobody who teaches here. That is the town being part of the sport rather than a beach with schools on it. What it does not settle is the Levante and the Poniente, which is the part you have to stand in.

evidence.what: the Global Kitesports Association's own event calendar

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. IKO Level 3 and then the instructor certification are a real, legible ladder with an outside body behind it — better than most crafts here. Its four levels are further down this page, in IKO's own words. We have read them; nobody of ours has climbed them.

new-basque-cuisine.verdict: A faculty the Basque chefs built for themselves, with their restaurants a few kilometres away — and a gap between the names on the page and the names in the classroom

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Named, with a caveat we would rather state than bury. Andoni Luis Aduriz at Mugaritz and Martín Berasategui at Lasarte-Oria are named on this page and both are real, working chefs in their own kitchens — but what they offer is a stage, not a course, and you apply rather than book. The Basque Culinary Center, which is where you can actually enrol, names no teacher on this page. Luis Irizar, who trained much of this generation, died in 2024 and now sits under 'where it comes from'.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at the faculty and shut at the restaurants, and the difference is the whole shape of this craft. The Basque Culinary Center runs its Culinary Techniques Mastery at about 3,320 EUR and the Escuela de Cocina Luis Irizar a two-year professional specialisation. Mugaritz and Berasategui take stagiaires on their own terms. Your hands can ruin it in either room.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: San Sebastián reads Legendary above, and the reason is not a school — it is that a town of a hundred and eighty thousand people holds one of the densest concentrations of serious kitchens in Europe, plus the faculty those kitchens founded. There is a generation above you here and one below, and they drink in the same bars.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes. San Sebastián Gastronomika fills the Kursaal in Donostia every autumn — 5–7 October in 2026 — a congress the city's own kitchens built and still fill. A town that hosts the argument about its cuisine is a town that cuisine belongs to. What we still have not done is walk the Gipuzkoa markets, which is where a week would teach more than the reading has.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. The Basque Culinary Center's degree is awarded with Mondragon University, which is an outside body with an examination behind it — one of the better ladders on this map. We have read it. We have not seen anyone climb it.

perfumery.verdict: Grasse publishes the bench you would stand at, and one of the names on it spent twelve years as the in-house perfumer at Hermès — we have still not been, so the last one is ours to earn

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Named, and unusually well: the Grasse Institute publishes its whole faculty. Jean-Claude Ellena teaches there — listed on their own page as 'Senior Perfumer – Ex Hermes', which undersells twelve years as that house's in-house perfumer — alongside senior perfumers Marianne Nawrocki and Joëlle Lerioux Patris and a bench of working perfumers. Versailles is the opposite and we say so on its entry: ISIPCA names no perfumer on the course page or on its own teams page. One city here tells you whose hands you would be watching. The other does not, and you should ask.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Wide, and unusually so for a craft with this reputation for being closed. The Grasse Institute of Perfumery runs an International Technical Degree in Fragrance Creation and Sensory Evaluation at about EUR 13,500; ISIPCA runs its summer school in Versailles; Cinquième Sens teaches in both cities; Molinard runs harvest-season workshops in Grasse. You book these. And your hands can ruin the work: an accord is a composition, and a wrong one is simply wrong.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Both destinations read Legendary on the community dots above, which are the evidence for this and not a second opinion. Grasse is a town organised around the industry, Versailles holds ISIPCA, and Givaudan runs its own four-year perfumery school in the same orbit. There is a generation above you here and one below.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and by the strongest source on this map. UNESCO inscribed “the skills related to perfume in Pays de Grasse” on its Representative List in 2018 — the growing of the plants, the processing of the raw materials and the composing, named together as one living practice belonging to that place. Grasse is fields as much as laboratories, which is why Molinard's workshops run at harvest and not in February. Standing in it in season is what the last dot still waits for.

evidence.what: UNESCO, Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, 2018

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. On paper the ladder is one of the best here — ISIPCA's diploma is state-recognised through the Université de Versailles, and the Grasse Institute's is an International Technical Degree, neither of them a certificate of attendance. That is what their pages say and we believe it. We have not seen anyone finish.

photography.verdict: The schools here are among the best in the world and we cannot tell you who teaches at a single one of them — that is our gap, not theirs, and it is the first thing to fix on this page

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Empty across all four cities, and it is our failing rather than the craft's. Spéos, Gobelins, the International Center of Photography, the ENSP at Arles, the RCA, Central Saint Martins — and not one named teacher between them on this page. Magnum's Arles workshops are taught by Magnum photographers, whose names are public. This is closeable research, not an absence in the world, and until it is closed you should ask each school who will actually be in the room.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at every level and on published dates: Spéos runs a one-year professional programme in Paris at 18,950 EUR for EU students and 20,950 for international, ICP a one-year certificate in New York, the ENSP a three-year master-level diploma at Arles, and the Rencontres d'Arles run two- to six-day workshops each spring and summer. Your hands can ruin it in the ordinary way of the craft — the frame you did not take is gone.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: New York reads Legendary on the community dots above and Paris, Arles and London all read Thriving. Arles in particular is a scene that assembles: the Rencontres bring the working world of the craft to one town for a season, which is a different and rarer thing than a school with good rooms.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, in Paris. Paris Photo takes the Grand Palais for four days each November — 12–15 November in 2026 — and it is the largest fair in the world for the photography market. A city that hosts the trade's own market is a city the craft lives in, not one that happens to have schools. ⚠ Arles is the more obvious answer and we are not using it: the festival there runs workshops we list on this page, so it cannot be its own witness.

evidence.what: Paris Photo, at the Grand Palais

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and the ladder is real on paper — the ENSP diploma is master-level, the RCA and Central Saint Martins award MAs, and ICP's certificate is read in the trade. We have read that. We have not watched anyone climb it.

sushi-and-washoku.verdict: Everything a stranger needs is here and published — teachers by name, courses in English, dates and prices — and we have still not stood at any of these counters, so the last two are ours to earn

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Named, and recently better named. Tokyo Sushi Academy publishes all seven of its instructors — Fumimasa Murakami is vice-principal, and Sachiko Goto and Kumiko Imazu carry the International Sushi Course, the one taught for people who do not speak Japanese. And Hiroko Ishii, who was one of the two main instructors of that same English course, has opened her own school: JCMA in Bunkyo-ku, eight students to a room. Jiro Ono used to sit in this field on this page. He teaches at none of these schools, and taking his name out of it is what let the real ones in.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Wide open, on dates, in English, which is rarer in this craft than the teaching. Tokyo Sushi Academy has run international courses since 2002. JCMA's diploma is six weeks in three levels — knife work and shari, then whole-fish butchery and counter service, then anago, hirame and the structure of an omakase — at 1,200,000 JPY, and they will help with the student visa. Your hands can ruin it in front of people: the final exam is serving omakase at the counter.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Tokyo reads Legendary on the community dots above, and the evidence is the ordinary fact of the city: the market, the counters, and schools that have put thousands of foreign cooks through since 2002. There is a generation above you here and one below, and both are at work by five in the morning.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: We have not been. That is the whole reason this one is empty — not anything we found. This craft belongs to its place about as completely as any on the map, and one morning at Toyosu with somebody who buys there would answer it.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: The same reason. On paper the ladder is real and unusually legible — Japan has a national cooking licence, and JCMA's third level ends in a Diploma in Professional Sushi Arts rather than a certificate of attendance. We have read that. We have not watched anyone climb it, and one of these schools is three months old.

_measureCaps_comment: How far the evidence lets a craft's dots go. THE GROUND and THE STRETCH cannot be answered from a website, so desk research stops at three. One person who was actually there lifts it — but one visit is one week and one cohort, so five is held back for a place that held up more than once. Arnaud, 2 Sept 2026: one vouch for now. To let a single visit go all the way to five, change stood-in/vouched to 5 here; nothing else moves. ⭐ 3 Sept 2026: 'public evidence on the place' lifts the desk cap to four when the FOURTH condition is carried by a source that is not selling the course — a guild, a festival, a market, a trade body, a listing. Arnaud: 'most of the places the craft is alive their.' The build computes every host that sells a course on the craft and refuses evidence from any of them, and the FIFTH condition is still uncappable from a desk: a ladder proves the rungs exist, not that the room above you is worth years.
_measureDebt_comment: Arnaud, 2 Sept 2026: 'make it the standard of ET any skill sheet that comes out.' These crafts opened before the Measure existed; failing on them would only get the rule deleted, so the archive is a printed backlog. But the debt MAY NOT GROW — a new sheet with no grade pushes the count past the floor and stops the build. Grade one, lower the floor, and it can never drift back up. measureDebtKnown exists only so the error can name the new craft.
_skillLadders_comment: The ladder a craft is climbed by — ALWAYS somebody else's published standard, adopted and cited, never ours. 112 of 113 crafts carry a certBody and a goldCredential, so the ladder usually exists in public; where no body publishes one, the craft goes in laddersNotPublished and shows no ladder, because an invented rung is this map awarding itself an authority it does not have. A rung is the unit a course is ticked against, and the body's own skills are printed under it as what the rung means: IKO lists 46 skills across four levels and a kite school's page says 'we take you to Level 2', so ticking skills would have measured what a school writes on its website. url + read + verify on the ladder and on every rung, because night-check.py re-reads all of them.

_courseCoverage_comment: What each school PUBLISHES about which rungs its teaching covers — read off their own page, on a date, with their own wording kept as `verify` so night-check.py re-reads it. Never a score and never sorted: the order is the order the schools are already in. ⚠ Cite the page the syllabus is actually ON — Freeride Tarifa's home page names no level and its lessons page publishes the whole IKO syllabus, and a verify string is only checked against the url the entry gives. ⚠ Every rung is either ticked or given a reason (not-named · not-taught-here · above-this-course); the build refuses a partial list. A school we could not read gets no entry at all — an absence, not a zero.

laddersNotPublished.photography: Its own certifying line on this map reads 'ICP / Spéos / no universal body (portfolio + diploma)'. There is no ladder to adopt: photography is judged on a portfolio, and inventing rungs for it would be us awarding ourselves a standard nobody asked us to write.

_laddersNotPublished_comment: Crafts where NO body publishes a ladder — declared, so the debt count does not treat them as work owed and nobody quietly writes rungs for them later. The reason is the craft's own certBody saying so.
_ladderDebt_comment: The ratchet, same as measureDebtFloor: the archive of crafts with no ladder is printed, not fatal, but it MAY NOT GROW. A craft opening without one stops the build and names itself. Lower the floor whenever it falls, so it can never drift back up.
